key_information_units.information: Coop Pank's net profit decreased to €28.7 million in 2025, a 11% year-on-year decline, driven by lower interest rates. Net interest income fell to €73.3 million from €77.6 million, while return on equity dropped to 12.9% from 16.2% and cost-to-income ratio rose to 52.3% from 49.6%.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Financial results table; Managing Director´s Statement

key_information_units.information: The loan portfolio grew by 19% to €2.11 billion in 2025, with business loans increasing by 27% (€207m) and home loans by 17% (€125m).
key_information_units.source_evidence: Managing Director´s Statement; Financial results table

key_information_units.information: Customer deposits increased by 9% to €2.05 billion in 2025, comprising €1.41 billion term deposits and €0.64 billion demand deposits.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Managing Director´s Statement; Financial results table

key_information_units.information: The customer base grew by 9% to 227,000 customers in 2025, with 16,000 new private and 3,000 new business customers.
key_information_units.source_evidence: Managing Director´s Statement (Increase in the number of customers section)

key_information_units.information: Coop Pank targets to increase its loan market share to 10% by 2030 and double net profit to at least €60 million by 2030, aiming for annual growth 2-3 times faster than the market average.
The bank's Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio was 14.15% at end-2025, with total capital adequacy ratio at 18.54%, meeting all regulatory requirements.

In 2025, Coop Pank issued €250 million covered bonds on the Irish stock exchange (Q1 2025) and entered a guarantee agreement with the European Investment Bank Group (Dec 2025) to provide up to €249 million in new loans.

Post-reporting period, Coop Pank drew down a €5 million subordinated loan from the European Energy Efficiency Fund in February 2026 and appointed Alvar Pihlapuu to the Management Board in January 2026.

Coop Pank enhanced digital services by introducing virtual cards and expanded its branch network (opening in Valga and Viljandi), while launching a cashback program paying 1% on Coop store purchases via debit cards, totaling €270,000 in 2025.
Coop Pank's carbon footprint decreased to 212,758 tCO2e in 2025 from 248,855 tCO2e in 2024, with financing of solar and wind parks accounting for about 3.8% of the corporate financing portfolio.
